speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me when you first noticed the swelling and pain in your right ring finger? Also, have you experienced any recent injury or trauma to that area?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information; the mechanism of injury you described is consistent with a "jersey finger" or tendon avulsion. Can you tell me if you are currently unable to bend your right ring finger at the distal joint, or if the finger is stuck in an extended position?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the injury mechanism and your inability to bend the fingertip, I suspect a jersey finger, which is an avulsion of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon. Do you feel a palpable lump or mass in the palm of your hand where the tendon might have retracted?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant medical history. Social history: Student and active in sports, particularly football. Non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any numbness or tingling in the finger, and has the swelling spread to the rest of your hand? REQUEST TEST: X-Ray Right Hand.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: X-ray of the Right Hand: No bone fractures or dislocations visible. Soft tissue swelling noted around the distal interphalangeal joint of the right ring finger. Neurovascular Assessment: Normal capillary refill, no sensory deficits (no numbness or tingling reported).

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on the mechanism of injury, your inability to flex the fingertip, and the X-ray ruling out a fracture, the clinical picture strongly suggests a flexor digitorum profundus tendon avulsion. I would like to confirm the location of the retracted tendon before finalizing the plan. Can you feel a lump or bump in the palm of your right hand?

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, numbness, or tingling in the affected finger.

speaker: Doctor
text: You mentioned denying numbness, but did you feel a palpable lump or bump in your palm where the tendon might have retracted? If not, I will proceed with the diagnosis based on the clinical findings and X-ray results. DIAGNOSIS READY: Jersey Finger (Flexor Digitorum Profundus Tendon Avulsion).

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
